correctness.rationale: For k>=2, alpha>0,beta>=0,eta>0, independent noise makes the finite chain irreducible and leaf permutations make the hub/count projection exact. Applying the generator to a product of r distinct leaf bits and its hub product yields the positive-denominator triangular recurrences. Binomial-polynomial inversion recovers all finite hub/count probabilities. A compact stationary generator limit and moment determinacy establish the beta asymptotic. The seven-file package includes a self-contained exact verifier, which independently re-solves and compares all joint probabilities on 30 rational chains with 2550 assertions. Computation does not substitute for the all-k analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Within the inspected literature and own prior claim record, the primary contribution is the complete exact finite-k stationary hub/count distribution from an all-order forward triangular factorial-moment closure and binomial inversion. Cox–Peres–Steif give the same reduced chain for mixing, not the full joint law. Earlier own two-point discounted star discord yields second-order conclusions through duality, but does not give the full finite joint law or higher factorial moments. General noisy-voter duality and inaccessible historical full text remain genuine priority risks.

value.rationale: The natural full stationary distribution of a heterogeneous star-noisy-voter process is computed exactly for every finite degree and positive rate, using a forward moment hierarchy rather than exponential configuration enumeration. This yields all stationary count and hub-conditioned probabilities, beyond pair covariances, and supports finite-versus-large-network uncertainty comparisons. The statement has structural and reproducibility value without asserting a new noisy voter model, a new limiting PDMP law, or policy-level realism.
